summary: No control area or Article 4 direction for holiday lets. A 2018 council report said most short lets in Bath (3 or fewer rooms) stay in the C3 home use class; larger ones can be a material change of use.

The council says most Airbnb-style holiday lets need planning permission: self-contained holiday flats and houses with no on-site management are a sui generis use. Outside the Town Centre, Resort Core and 6 Holiday Accommodation Areas, permission "generally will not be granted".

A 2026 Full Council motion asks officers to investigate whether homes let for more than 90 nights a year are a material change of use and to gather evidence for a possible Article 4 direction. Nothing decided.
The council says you might need permission depending on how much the use changes. Zones where short lets are allowed or restricted are being looked at for City Plan 2041; nothing new applies yet.
Draft Local Plan 2022-2040 Policy H2 would refuse the loss of an existing home, with narrow exceptions; adoption expected late 2026. Whether the main modifications change H2: UNVERIFIED.

Local Plan 2018 Policy 3 allows changing housing to other uses only in exceptional circumstances; in Jan 2018 officers recommended enforcement notices against 13 flats used as short-term visitor accommodation. Draft Greater Cambridge Local Plan Policy J/VA would go further (not in force).

No short-let control area or Article 4 direction for holiday lets found. England has no short-let use class, so the council decides case by case whether letting a whole home is a material change of use.
